title: Lesson 1: String Gallop
lessonSummary: Your messages now gallop along – f-strings glue text and variables together in one go!

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at how the values are filled into the text.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse_name = "Thunder"
age = 8
print(f"Hello {horse_name}!")
print(f"You are {age} years old!")

feed_morning = 3
feed_evening = 2
print(f"Daily feed: {feed_morning + feed_evening} kg")

tasks.instruction: The variables rider and horse are already there. Use an f-string to print exactly this sentence: Sarah rides Luna today.
Create feed_morning = 4 and feed_evening = 3. Use an f-string with a calculation inside the braces to print exactly: Daily feed: 7 kg

title: Lesson 2: Walk and Trot – str and int
lessonSummary: Text and whole numbers are no secret to you any more – and type() tells you which is which!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: text is a walk (str), a whole number is a trot (int).
tasks.codeTemplate:
horse_name = "Windstorm"
breed = "Hanoverian"
print(f"Horse: {horse_name}")
print(f"Breed: {breed}")
print(f"Type: {type(horse_name)}")

age = 7
height_cm = 168
print(f"Age: {age} years, Height: {height_cm} cm")
print(f"Type: {type(age)}")

tasks.instruction: Create a variable height_cm = 168 and use type() to print its type with print().
The variable breed is already there. Print exactly this line with an f-string: Type of breed: <class 'str'>  (do not type the type yourself – let type() find it!)

title: Lesson 3: Canter and Jump – float and bool
lessonSummary: Decimal numbers and yes/no values – now you know all four hoofbeat types!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: canter (float) and jump (bool).
tasks.codeTemplate:
weight = 550.5
feed_amount = 4.25
print(f"Weight: {weight} kg, Feed: {feed_amount} kg")
print(f"Type: {type(weight)}")

has_saddle = True
is_visited = False
print(f"Has saddle: {has_saddle}")
print(f"Type: {type(has_saddle)}")

print(f"Is 5 greater than 3? {5 > 3}")

tasks.instruction: Create weight = 550.5 and print exactly this line with an f-string: Weight type: <class 'float'>
Create has_saddle = True and print exactly this line with an f-string: Saddle type: <class 'bool'>

title: Lesson 4: Calculating with Numbers
lessonSummary: Feed calculations, stable planning – Python is your calculator!

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look closely at the result of the division.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses_a = 12
horses_b = 8
print(f"Total horses: {horses_a + horses_b}")
print(f"Difference: {horses_a - horses_b}")
print(f"Double stables: {horses_a * 2}")
print(f"Horses per box: {horses_a / 4}")

tasks.instruction: The variables horses and boxes are already there. Print exactly this line: Horses per box: 3.0 (let Python calculate it!)
Create feed = 7 and print exactly this line, with the calculation inside the braces: Double feed: 14 kg

title: Lesson 5: Working with Text
lessonSummary: Joining and repeating texts – now the stable even whinnies on command!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: joining and repeating texts.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = "Star"
suffix = "light"
full_name = name + suffix
print(f"Full name: {full_name}")
print(f"Whinny: {name * 3}")

tasks.instruction: The variables first and second are already there. Join them with + and print exactly: Thunderbolt
Create sound = "Neigh! " (with a space at the end) and print the sound three times with one print() and the * sign.

title: Lesson 6: Converting Types – int(), float(), str(), bool()
lessonSummary: You can turn any type into another – with four handy functions!

tasks.instruction: Run this example and compare the types before and after converting.
tasks.codeTemplate:
age_text = "5"
age_number = int(age_text)
print(f"Age as text: {age_text} (type: {type(age_text)})")
print(f"Age as number: {age_number} (type: {type(age_number)})")

print(float("4.25") * 2)
print(str(12) + " horses")
print(bool(0))
print(bool("Thunder"))

tasks.instruction: The variable price_text holds the text "4.5". Convert it with float() and print exactly: Double price: 9.0
The variable count is already there. Use str() and + to print exactly: Horses: 12  (no f-string this time!)

title: Lesson 7: Processing Input
lessonSummary: Whatever a rider types in arrives as text – now you know how to turn it into numbers!

print(f"Entry type: {type(entry)}")
